subject: Priority playbook + exception-closure matrix — QBR inputs
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Priority playbook + exception-closure matrix — QBR inputs

Team —

Kicking off a short thread to capture commitments and clarify exec asks for the upcoming QBR. I attached a first-pass priority matrix (priority_matrix_v2.xlsx) and the raw exceptions tracker (exceptions_tracker.csv). Goal: have owners + ETA for each line by Friday EOD (2028-08-11) so I can fold into the QBR deck.

Three specific asks from the execs:
- Top-3 roadmap items they want visible (impact, owner, risk).
- Any open exceptions that require SLA/credits or product trade-offs to resolve.
- One fallback plan per risky item (short-term mitigation if primary fix slips).

Quick summary of where I see things (high-level):
1) Query batching for Dedicated — product asks: tighten tail latency for 512+ tokens (owner: Lauren). Risk: kernel availability/quantization edge cases.
2) Prefix cache consistency — product asks: stable KV snapshotting for private deployments (owner: Rishi). Risk: perf regression on long sequences.
3) Autoscale policy for reserved pools — product asks: predictable burst capacity without overprovisioning (owner: Vivek). Risk: cloud quota and budget exposure.

Please: reply with the owner line(s) you accept, an ETA (date) for a delivery or mitigation, and whether you need cross-team help (ops/security/legal). If you want me to raise a fast-track exec ask (credits/exception), say so and why.

Attachments: priority_matrix_v2.xlsx (matrix), exceptions_tracker.csv (raw export).

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. PM, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 7 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority playbook + exception-closure matrix — QBR inputs

Thanks, Mateo — taking ownership of #1 (query batching tail latency) and I'll pair with infra to prototype a guarded kernel fallback.

ETA: Proof-of-concept by 2028-08-18, validated on a small reserved pool by 2028-08-25.

Question: for the exec ask on "tighten tail latency for 512+ tokens", do they want a hard SLO target (p99 < X ms) or a qualitative improvement? Having a numeric target helps engineering prioritize across competing kernel maintenance work.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Aug 2028 07:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priority playbook + exception-closure matrix — QBR inputs

Lauren — +1 on numeric SLO. For context, the main technical blocker for a hard p99 target is quantization-induced variance on long sequences when the new optimized kernels first land. I ran a quick sim and attached a short note (kv-cache-impact.pdf) — shows p95 improvements but p99 volatility under adversarial sequence mixes.

Proposal: two-phase plan
- Phase A (short-term mitigation): guarded kernel with fallback to current stable path when we detect KV instability. Implementation scope: ~10 dev-weeks across runtime and QA. Target: 2028-08-25 for guarded rollout to canary.
- Phase B (long-term): kernel rework + quantization tuning; target: 2028-10-05.

I can own Phase A implementation if infra can allocate 2 FTEs for 3 weeks for performance validation. If we cannot get the infra headcount, we should mark this as "Requires exec approval" for temporary burst capacity or contractor support.

Thanks for the note and for sharing the matrix. From a Nimbus perspective the top priority is query stability for long-document analytics (the same as your #1). Our ask: if there's any chance this slips past September we need a temporary SLA commitment from Redwood on time-to-notify for regressions and an operational contact. We can escalate contractually if needed.

We're available for a 30-minute sync next week if that helps.

Subject: RE: Priority playbook + exception-closure matrix — QBR inputs

Thanks for the fast responses — consolidating as promised. Below is the action ledger I will present in the QBR pack. Please confirm inline if anything is off.

Action ledger (owner / ETA / blockers / exec ask?)
- Query batching tail latency — owner: Lauren Bishop / ETA: 2028-08-25 (canary) / blocker: infra FTE for validation / exec ask: approve 2 FTE short-term or contractor budget.
- Prefix KV snapshotting — owner: Rishi Malhotra / ETA: Phase A guarded rollout 2028-08-25, Phase B full fix 2028-10-05 / blocker: perf validation and regression window / exec ask: none today, but may need temporary extra reserved capacity during rollout.
- Reserved pool autoscale policy — owner: Vivek Kulkarni / ETA: 2028-09-08 / blocker: cloud quota limits / exec ask: temporary quota bump for pilot.
- Exceptions closure: customer-impacting rows flagged in exceptions_tracker.csv — owner: Tessa Morgan / ETA: 2028-08-14 / blocker: legal sign-off on customer credits / exec ask: one-off credit approval if high-impact.

Next steps:
- Lauren/Rishi: confirm the 2028-08-25 canary date and whether you can live with numeric p99 target (suggested p99 < 1200ms for 512+ tokens).
- Vivek: confirm quota bump request & rough numbers so I can open a formal cloud quota ticket.
- Tessa: mark any rows that need immediate exec credit approval and give me the estimated $ amount.

I will incorporate confirmations into the QBR deck and circulate a draft (QBR_exec_asks_draft.docx) by Monday EOD. If anyone needs a quick call to reconcile trade-offs, I can schedule 30m.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. PM, Platform
Redwood Inference
Attachments: QBR_exec_asks_draft.docx
